One fix for the id at the trait's declaration would retire the workaround; then the conformance site. (2) decide whether the declared-entry leg should also refuse a sibling's import of a different program (B226's rule applied per leg) or file mode should accept it; pin whichever.

items.title: NEW — a struct parameter reachable ONLY through another parameter's bound never grounds (`struct Held<T> { list: Signal<List<T>> }` leaves `T = any`), and the written form ACCEPTS `Held<i32, SignalCell<List<str>>>`: the bound is not checked against the written arguments at a struct's parameter list (UNSOUND)

Pins: the hidden-parameter form grounding `T`, the written form refusing `Held<i32, SignalCell<List<str>>>`, a bounded-and-satisfied control.

items.title: NEW — a bare trait in RETURN position (`fun f(): Trait`): the last value position that refuses; the case each way
items.discussion: b184-b218's question; OWNER decision; `fun get(): C` for a sugared struct is a SEPARATE, harder question
items.body: AGAINST: it is the existential (the callee picks) where B161/B186/B184 are all universal (the caller picks) — one bare spelling meaning two quantifiers by which side of the colon it is on; vilan has no opaque-type kind and would need one, plus a refusal for a callee with two `ret` arms at two impls; today's refusal costs one written generic. FOR: the surface reads "bare trait works everywhere except here"; it removes a real cascade (B252); it is the shape kolt reached for. Also on the item: should `C<A>` ever be WRITABLE (today "takes 0 type arguments", deliberately); and whether the attributed-declaration carve-out (`[derive]`/`[service]` cannot spell a hidden parameter) closes by teaching meta.vl about hidden parameters.

items.title: NEW — `async_infer::dispatch_candidates` still resolves `OnType(Some(receiver), member)` against EVERY same-named member when the receiver is KNOWN (only the `_for` call sites narrow): the miscoloring class a49-async fixed for trait default bodies, reachable via an inherited default on a concrete value
items.discussion: lane a49-async's find (the merged-tree async regression's sibling)
items.body: The fix narrowed `OnType(None, member)` (a `self` call inside a trait default body) to the trait's own subjects — supertraits closed downward, nominal heads, blankets via `subject_applies`. Apply the same subject-based narrowing inside `dispatch_candidates` for a known receiver, and note that `call_graph.rs` and `init_order.rs` read the same set (the narrowing removes bogus reachability edges — strictly more accurate). Pins: an inherited default on a concrete value beside an unrelated same-named async inherent member; the genuinely-async control.
